title: Durably reducing conspiracy beliefs through dialogues with AI

paper.authors: Thomas H. Costello, Gordon Pennycook, David G. Rand
paper.repo: data: Dryad https://doi.org/10.5061/dryad.v6wwpzh4h ; analysis code: Zenodo https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.12751761 (Primary_Analyses RMD/HTML, Natural_Language_Processing.zip)

dependence.note: The LLM is the intervention: it generated the persuasive, evidence-based counter-arguments in a three-round dialogue with each participant. The measured outcome is human belief change, so the model output is a necessary component but not the outcome itself.

claim.statement: Personalised evidence-based dialogues with GPT-4 Turbo reduced participants' belief in their chosen conspiracy theory by ~20% relative to control (2,190 participants across two studies), an effect that persisted 2 months later and generalised to unrelated conspiracies and behavioural intentions (abstract; main-effect figure/table number not verifiable from the paywalled text).
claim.metric: pre-to-post change in belief in the personalised conspiracy (0-100 scale; columns Pre_Belief_Specific / Post_Belief_Specific / DV_BeliefChange_Specific in the Dryad codebook) in the AI-dialogue arm vs control; follow-ups at 10 days and 2 months; BCTI for generalisation

original_values.per_study_n_cohens_d_factcheck_share: NOT VERIFIED - the Science full text and supplementary materials are paywalled/blocked for our fetcher; the PsyArXiv PDF download returned HTTP 403. Do not cite d or the fact-checker percentages until read from the paper.

protocol.evaluation: Human-rated core outcome (participants' own belief ratings) - NOT re-measurable without new participants. Model-side quantities that could be re-measured from the archived conversations: (a) regenerate the AI's three turns for each archived participant opener and compare content/strategy with the archived AI turns (embedding similarity; strategy ratings as in AI_Strategy_Ratings_2024-04-30.csv); (b) factual accuracy of the regenerated claims - but the original audit used a professional fact-checker (human), so (b) also needs new human labour.

baseline_alive.note: none confirmed; if the SM reveals gpt-4-turbo-2024-04-09, a model-side regeneration arm becomes possible

budget.assumptions: model-side proxy ONLY (not a claim re-run): regenerate 3 AI turns for each of 2,190 archived openers x 3 seeds; ~1,500 input tokens per turn (system prompt + participant statement + prior turns), ~300 output tokens. A 200-participant subsample would cost ~$43. No human-outcome re-measurement is included.

judgment.rule: Not judgeable under ANALYSIS_PLAN section 1 for the core claim (human belief change). If a model-side proxy is approved, judge only the proxy (e.g. direction and magnitude of strategy/content similarity, or fact-check accuracy on a human-audited subsample) and label it as such; the belief-reduction effect itself is right-censored/unmeasurable.
judgment.notes: Any successor-model dialogue effect would require a new human study (IRB, ~2,000 participants); out of scope.

user_checks: Can you read the Science text/SM (institutional access) and record: exact GPT-4 Turbo snapshot, temperature, system prompt, Study 1/2 Ns, Cohen's d, and the fact-checker audit numbers?

Is a model-side proxy (regenerate AI turns for a 200-participant subsample, ~$43, plus a human fact-check of a claim sample) worth budgeting, or should this paper be recorded as 'human-outcome, not re-executable'?
Please download Data_8.28.24.zip and README.md from Dryad (our fetcher is blocked) if the proxy is approved.
domain_notes: Landmark persuasion study: the LLM's value lies in tailoring evidence to each participant's specific conspiracy and stated evidence; the outcome is a within-person belief change on a 0-100 scale with 10-day and 2-month follow-ups. The AI's factual accuracy was audited by a professional fact-checker (share reported in the paper - to be verified). Reproducing the effect on successors is a human-subjects study, not an API re-run; only dialogue-content drift can be measured cheaply.
